resolutions.researcher_notes: Value 12,4,16 in matches the MGS-3 package 12 (Eastern/Qassim) scope. MEED (independent trade journalism): 'laying of 16-inch, 12-inch and 4-inch lateral pipelines in the Eastern Province and Qassim region clusters, covering a total distance of 116km.' Blackridge Research project profile independently lists package 12: 'Lay various diameter lateral pipelines (16-inch, 12-inch, 4-inch) in the Eastern Province and Qassim region (116km).' Two independent origins agree; no contradiction. Original brief current_ref (meed.com/aramco-selects-...) is actually live (200), not dead.

StartState/Province=Eastern (Province), EndPrefecture/District=Qassim, both Saudi Arabia. MEED: 'Eastern Province and Qassim region clusters.' Global Flow Control (quoting the GAS Arabian Tadawul disclosure): contract 'for the Master Gas System expansion in the East and Qassim clusters.' Two independent origins confirm the Eastern-Qassim corridor.

SegmentCost 111,000,000 USD confirmed. Global Flow Control: 'a contract valued at 416.3 million Saudi riyals ($111 million) for the Master Gas System expansion in the East and Qassim clusters.' Saudi Gulf Projects: 'valued at about SAR 416.3 million ... for the Master Gas System Expansion in East & Qassim Clusters.' MEED states 'The value of package 12 is $111m.' The Tadawul-disclosure reprints (Global Flow Control, Saudi Gulf Projects, Zawya) trace to the same GAS Arabian filing; MEED is an independent origin, so >=2 independent overall. No contradiction.

Owner1=Aramco 100%. Aramco is the client/owner of the Master Gas System; GAS Arabian Services is the EPC contractor (not owner). Both sources name Aramco as the awarding client for the MGS-3 Eastern/Qassim package. Consistent with Aramco 100% ownership of the MGS network; no contradiction.
